body:
## For the Owner

**What This Does:** Chete gets its own item in the menu bar, with Open Chete, Check for Updates and Quit, and no longer shows an icon in the Dock.

**Why:** Chete should open from wherever you are, as its plan says, and live in the menu bar rather than the Dock.

**Does It Change Your Apps?** Yes, once it is in a build you try: Chete leaves the Dock and appears in the menu bar. The keyboard shortcut comes later, because it must match the earlier Chete's.

**What to Do:** Approve it if you are happy: it changes how Chete appears on your Mac, so it needs your yes. Approve it before the welcome; the list of your copies can come before or after.

<details><summary>Checklist for the Agents</summary>

For #59

- [x] This closes exactly one issue, named above.
- [x] The test was written first and failed before the code, or this changes no code.
- [x] `Scripts/check` is green on my machine.
- [x] The reviewer agent read the newest commit and this description. Its reply is a comment here that names that commit, and each finding is fixed or answered there.
- [x] Nothing outside the slice was touched.

Shell gains `MenuBarItem`, a `MenuBarExtra` whose menu holds Open (`openWindow` then `NSApplication.activate()`), Check for Updates… and Quit. `CheteScene` gains one line, after `.commands`. Declared first, the menu-bar item stopped any window opening at launch (GitHub's tour on c820ef4), so it stays after Chete's window. #108 adds its welcome on the same line, so this merges first and #108 is then brought up to date. Look is not linked: the menu is the system's own. The tour was written first and failed on GitHub's Mac (Chete quit when its window closed, with nothing in the menu bar to keep it open); it now closes the window and opens it again from the item.

Not done: the keyboard shortcut, which must match the earlier Chete's and is not in this change yet. `UpdateCommands` stays for now, so this merges cleanly with #97; once Chete has no Dock icon it shows no menus of its own, so it can go in a later change. The update tour clicks an app's own menu, so the release after 1.0 will need it to use the menu-bar item instead.

</details>

latestReviews.body: It should have a little bit more pizzazz and, like, a menu bar card. Nothing too crazy or fancy, but just a nice little menu bar card that fits the overall theme, has some of the most recent copies on there, and a few buttons to navigate different parts of the UI, like the settings, or to quit the app. Just make it a little bit nicer, more than just a drop-down menu. It should be like a menu bar card.
